changelog: **Premium analytics is an entitlement now, not a setting** (#1740, epic #1727). The four `premiumAnalytics` gates — cohort comparison, source conversion, the cross-program benchmark and the weekly analytics report e-mail — plus the per-source split on the trial-conversion card ask `entitled(orgId, 'ADVANCED_ANALYTICS')` (#1733): the org's plan (Program and up) or an `OrgEntitlement` grant. A locked route answers `403 { error: 'feature_locked', code: 'feature_locked', feature: 'ADVANCED_ANALYTICS' }`. The benchmark still reads across orgs with its k-anonymity floor. `GET /api/admin/analytics/entitlements` (the no-probe read from #1442) now returns `{ advancedAnalytics, reportExport }` from `entitledFeatures()`; the client hook is `useAnalyticsEntitlements()` / `useAdvancedAnalytics()` in `src/lib/analyticsEntitlementsClient.ts`. The `premiumAnalytics` setting is gone — default, settings API, settings form and its EN/TR/DE strings. **Nobody loses access:** `prisma/backfill-premium-analytics-entitlement.mjs` (on every deploy, after the subscription backfill) grants a permanent `ADVANCED_ANALYTICS` to every org whose effective setting was `true` (tenant row → global row → default, the getSetting() rule, unit-tested) and then deletes the dead setting rows, so a re-run grants nothing — a surviving global `true` would otherwise leak the tier to every new org. The thirteen analytics specs switch the tier through a new `setOrgFeature()` / `setOrgFeatureFor(page)` helper instead of the settings API. The export route and the `REPORT_EXPORT` gate (the rest of #1740) follow separately.
